original_question: Let f : PN 99K PN be a dominant rational map de- fined over Q̄. (a) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f . The limit (15.3) defining αf (P ) converges. (b) The set αf (P ) : P ∈ PN (Q̄)f is finite. (c) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f . The arithmetic degree αf (P ) is an algebraic integer. (d) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f be a point whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Then αf (P ) = δf . Conjecture 15.3 is known for monomial maps, which are maps f = [f0 , . . . , fN ] such that their coordinate functions fi are monomials [215], and parts of the con- jecture are known in various other cases; see for example [128, 133, 134, 135]. We mayask for more refined information regarding the possible growth rates of h f n (P ) . The following is an arithmetic analogue of Question 14.16.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 15.3 (Arithmetic Degree Conjectures (on P^N)) in Section 15. The final sentence in the draft is the paper’s transition into Question 15.4, but the draft itself most closely matches Conjecture 15.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the Section 15 arithmetic-degree problem on projective space and reproduces the four clauses of Conjecture 15.3 in the right ambient setting f: P^N ⇢ P^N over Qbar: existence of α_f(P), finiteness of the set of arithmetic degrees, algebraic-integrality of α_f(P), and the equality α_f(P) = δ_f for points with Zariski-dense orbit. It also correctly keeps the hypothesis P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f and the Zariski-density condition in part (d).
missing_details: The draft is not stand-alone because it refers to '(15.3)' without writing out the definition α_f(P) = lim_{n→∞} h(f^n(P))^(1/n), where h is the logarithmic height on P^N(Qbar).

It does not define P^N(Qbar)_f, which in the paper means the set of points P whose entire forward orbit is well-defined, equivalently f^n(P) ∉ I(f) for all n ≥ 0, where I(f) is the indeterminacy locus.
It does not define the orbit notation O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n ≥ 0}.
It does not define the dynamical degree δ_f = lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n), which is essential for part (d).
It does not say explicitly that Qbar is the algebraic closure of Q.
It does not explain that the conjecture is stated for dominant rational maps on projective space P^N; one should not replace this by the broader smooth-projective-variety version Conjecture 15.9.
It should make clear that no extra degree hypothesis such as deg(f) ≥ 2 is assumed here; the paper states Conjecture 15.3 for any dominant rational self-map of P^N.
Because f is a rational map, not necessarily a morphism, the requirement P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f is essential and should not be omitted.
If full background precision is desired, 'Zariski dense in P^N' should be left explicit as in the paper, rather than paraphrased by a looser term such as 'generic orbit'.

The sentences about monomial maps and 'The following is an arithmetic analogue of Question 14.16' are contextual remarks after Conjecture 15.3 and before Question 15.4; they are not part of the conjecture itself.
refined_question: Let f: P^N ⇢ P^N be a dominant rational map defined over Qbar, let I(f) denote its indeterminacy locus, let P^N(Qbar)_f := {P ∈ P^N(Qbar) : f^n(P) ∉ I(f) for all n ≥ 0}, let O_f(P) := {f^n(P) : n ≥ 0}, let h be the logarithmic Weil height on P^N(Qbar), define the arithmetic degree (when it exists) by α_f(P) := lim_{n→∞} h(f^n(P))^(1/n), and define the dynamical degree by δ_f := lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n). Is it true that for every P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f: (i) the limit defining α_f(P) exists; (ii) the set {α_f(P) : P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f} is finite; (iii) each α_f(P) is an algebraic integer; and (iv) if O_f(P) is Zariski dense in P^N, then α_f(P) = δ_f?
justification: The draft matches Conjecture 15.3 almost verbatim. In Section 15, the paper first defines height and arithmetic degree, then states the inequality ᾱ_f(P) ≤ δ_f, and immediately afterward gives Conjecture 15.3 with exactly the four parts appearing in the draft. The draft’s last sentence is not part of Conjecture 15.3; it is the paper’s transition from Conjecture 15.3 to Question 15.4. To make the problem fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the definitions of h, α_f(P), P^N(Qbar)_f, O_f(P), and δ_f from the nearby context and earlier sections.
